about: resend's decision table (the P3 procedure). Every served operation is a handler: each request acts for the team its key belongs to (the front, around.ts), which the derived core does not model. Emails and domains carry state moves (last_event, status) the clock and the doors drive; the audience-scoped contact paths no application here calls are unmodeled, and every other operation is the vendor's gap.

decisions.demand: Dub, Twenty, Postiz and Twin's platform send their mail
decisions.why: an action: the send checked as Resend checks it (required fields, at most 50 recipients, the sender's verified domain or the testing domain to the team's own address), kept, and moved queued to sent (email.sent); the recipient's server takes or refuses it on the clock; Twenty attachments retain blob bytes and Dub scheduled_at waits on the vendor clock before sending

decisions.demand: Dub's and Twenty's batches
decisions.why: an action: up to 100 sends, each checked first so one refused refuses the batch, then each kept and sent as one send is

decisions.demand: Twenty reads a sent email
decisions.why: the team's own email only (another team's answers 404), shown as Resend answers it without the kernel's bookkeeping

decisions.demand: The vendor's published List Emails example and the vendor-backed root's refresh of emails
decisions.why: the team's emails newest first, paged by limit, after and before as Resend pages, each in the List Emails page's shape (no bodies, empty cc, bcc and reply_to as null)

decisions.demand: Twenty reads an inbound reply and downloads its raw message
decisions.why: the team's received email with raw.download_url, a pre-signed URL on the inbound CDN for an hour, which the inbound-cdn screen answers

decisions.demand: Dub, Twenty and the Postiz cookbook add a sending domain
decisions.why: an action: a name registered anywhere refused, the region checked, the DKIM, SPF (and tracking and receiving) records made for the owner's DNS host, status not_started

decisions.demand: Dub and Twenty read a domain's records and status
decisions.why: the team's own domain only, with its records and their statuses

decisions.demand: Twenty and the Postiz cookbook find a domain by name; the vendor-backed root's refresh of domains
decisions.why: the team's domains newest first without their records, paged by limit, after and before

decisions.demand: Dub's queued job sets open tracking, click tracking and TLS after a domain's creation
decisions.why: the team's own domain only: tracking, TLS, tracking subdomain and capabilities changed, the Tracking and Receiving records following them; the id answered

decisions.demand: Dub, Twenty and the Postiz cookbook start a domain's verification
decisions.why: a state move: not_started, failed or pending to pending (a verified domain stays verified); the clock verifies it once its records are at the owner's DNS host, or fails it after 72 hours

decisions.demand: Dub and Twenty remove a domain renamed or deleted
decisions.why: the team's own domain only, removed, its id answered with deleted true

decisions.demand: every application's key, made on the API Keys page
decisions.why: Resend's API makes a key only with a full-access key already held; the first key of a team is made on the dashboard

decisions.demand: the life's deleted key refused 403
decisions.why: a key deleted on the API Keys page

decisions.demand: the World's application's RESEND_API_KEY (the descriptor's credentialDoor)
decisions.why: the runtime issues the application's key at every boot, as the dashboard would

decisions.demand: Dub's and Twenty's webhook endpoints
decisions.why: an endpoint added on the Webhooks page, with its signing secret; the applications take the events they handle there

decisions.demand: a domain's verification (Dub, Twenty, the Postiz cookbook)
decisions.why: the owner sets the domain's records at their DNS host, outside Resend

decisions.demand: Dub's and Twenty's email.bounced
decisions.why: whether an outside mail server refuses mail for its domain, outside Resend

decisions.demand: Dub's email.opened
decisions.why: a recipient opens the email, outside Resend

decisions.demand: Twenty's email.complained
decisions.why: a recipient marks the email as spam, outside Resend

decisions.demand: Twenty's email.received and inbound reply
decisions.why: mail sent from outside to an address at a receiving domain

decisions.demand: the Postiz cookbook's inbox, and every life step that reads what a recipient got
decisions.why: what reached a recipient's inbox, outside Resend

decisions.demand: what Dub's and Twenty's endpoints were sent
decisions.why: the webhooks Resend sent to an endpoint, as its receiver saw them

decisions.demand: A vendor-backed root enumerates received mail before retrieving its full message
decisions.why: The reference offers a whole-account received-email list. Refresh must enumerate it rather than treating received mail as bookkeeping or using only known ids.
